worldBible.title: Velvet Static
worldBible.logline: When a citywide radio built from living coral begins broadcasting tomorrow's memories, a disgraced costume conservator must decode its songs before a vanished district is sung permanently out of existence.

setting.name: Aster Coil
setting.description: A tidal metropolis of lacquered theaters, salt tramlines, and apartment reefs hums around a cathedral-sized radio organism rooted in the harbor floor.
setting.era: retro-futurist interwar age with biotech craft

protagonist.name: Ione Vey
protagonist.role: costume conservator for the Ministry of Pageants
protagonist.description: Sharp-fingered and scent-obsessed, she restores garments woven with conductive thread and hears flaws in fabric the way other people hear lies.
protagonist.motivation: She wants to recover her erased sister and prove that memory can be mended rather than curated into silence.

supportingCharacters.name: Brother Mneme
supportingCharacters.description: A serene heretic with ink-black lungs, he maps emotional frequencies by listening to preserved throats in glass reliquaries.
supportingCharacters.relationToProtagonist: He becomes Ione's uneasy research partner and tempts her toward dangerous truths.

supportingCharacters.name: Lark Hush
supportingCharacters.role: deaf nightclub percussionist and signal smuggler
supportingCharacters.description: She reads vibration through silver cane tips and runs contraband broadcasts beneath the city's official music curfew.
supportingCharacters.relationToProtagonist: She is Ione's ex-lover and most reliable route into the outlaw airwaves.

supportingCharacters.name: Provost Sable Mire
supportingCharacters.role: director of the Ministry of Pageants
supportingCharacters.description: Velvet-voiced and immaculate, he stages civic spectacles to edit public grief into obedience.
supportingCharacters.relationToProtagonist: He is Ione's patron turned censor, protecting the city by erasing what she seeks.

worldBible.centralConflict: As the harbor radio leaks tomorrow's memories into tonight, Ione must choose between restoring a lost district and unraveling the curated identity that keeps Aster Coil from panic.

scene.location: Aster Coil, rain-slick parade avenue above the harbor

script.text: Rain lashes the parade avenue and turns the brass tram rails into bright lines under your boots. Below the seawall, the harbor radio groans through the city. Each note from the Pelagic Choir shivers in your teeth. You are Ione Vey, a disgraced conservator, and you are running because the song just said your sister's name out loud.

Ahead, a staircase appears where there should only be a blank retaining wall. Water pours down its steps. Painted on the wall beside it, fresh gold Ministry arrows point people away as if the staircase does not matter. It matters to you because the voice from the harbor said your sister is waiting in the Drowned Quarter, in a district the city swears was never there.

script.speaker: Lark Hush
script.text: Don't go down blind. The broadcast is peaking. If the stairs are real tonight, they may not be real in five minutes.

Lark Hush, your ex-lover and signal ally, stands half under a torn awning with a drum case strapped across her back. Rain beads on her shaved scalp. Across the avenue, Ministry lanterns swing toward you in a tight line. Provost Sable Mire's people are sweeping the block before the crowd can see the staircase.

script.speaker: Brother Mneme
script.text: Choose fast, Ione. We can trace the song, save the evidence, or lose both.

choices.label: Run down the hidden staircase into the Drowned Quarter before the Ministry arrives
Go to Lark and use her smuggled gear to capture the broadcast first
Step into the avenue and confront the Ministry sweep before they seal the stairs

nodes.name: Ione Vey
nodes.description: A disgraced conservator with a tailor's ear for electrical fabric hunts what the city has deliberately forgotten.

nodes.name: Brother Mneme
nodes.description: A gentle apostate of sacred acoustics studies how memory nests inside flesh and song.

nodes.name: Lark Hush
nodes.description: A deaf percussionist smuggles forbidden frequencies through the city's drenched understage tunnels.

nodes.name: Provost Sable Mire
nodes.description: The Ministry's elegant master of ceremonies weaponizes pageantry to manage what the populace is allowed to remember.

nodes.name: Aster Coil
nodes.description: This glamorous salt-bright city loops around a living harbor radio whose songs stain the weather with prophecy.

nodes.name: The Pelagic Choir
nodes.description: A cathedral-sized coral radio breathes through brass pipes and broadcasts memories no one has lived yet.

nodes.name: The Ministry of Pageants
nodes.description: A civic arts bureau uses costume, parade, and spectacle to canonize acceptable history.

nodes.name: The Drowned Quarter
nodes.description: An entire district survives only as damp afterimages in people's habits, with staircases leading to addresses no map admits.

nodes.name: Tomorrow's Memory Broadcast
nodes.description: The harbor radio begins leaking future recollections that cause citizens to mourn events before they occur.

nodes.name: Memory Versus Curation
nodes.description: The city's survival depends on whether truth should be preserved whole or beautified into something bearable.
